Commentary.Commentary: That's it then for this series and it is South Africa who win it 2-0. The Proteas skipper, David Miller picks up the winners' trophy and he and his team celebrate and pose for a team photo. Both teams will now move on to a new challenge as Ireland welcome Afghanistan for a five-match T20I series starting the 9th of August. As for South Africa, they move their attention back on to England and gear up for the Test series starting on the 17th of August. Hope you enjoyed our coverage, until next time. Cheers!

David Miller, the captain of South Africa says that he is fit now and he had a back spasm during the first game. Adds that it is a good problem to have when everyone is performing and it is great and healthy to see the guys performing well. Says that it is really nice to contribute as a captain and he has seen a lot of different facets of the game while doing captaincy. Mentions that the last 18 months have been pretty good for them and certainly they will be a force in the upcoming T20 World cup but don't won't to get ahead of themselves.

The Irish skipper, Andy Balbirnie is down for a chat. He says that it wasn’t as close as it looks on the scoreboard and says that after the first innings onslaught they were always chasing the game. Says the spinners bowled well in the beginning and kept them ahead in the game but towards the end, South Africa batted well and scored freely using the small boundaries to their advantage. He claims that they were still happy at the halfway mark and were looking to come out positively and chase down the total. He says that his team can not wait to get back on the horse and plan for the future with the five games against Afghanistan and the World Cup to look forward to.

Reeza Hendricks is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES for his exploits with the bat in both games. He says that the guys played pretty well today and he is happy to have contributed to the win. Adds that he tries to keep it as simple as possible and just play his game. Says that when setting a total, he tries to focus on taking it ball by ball and the end result will take care of itself.

Wayne Parnell (5 for 30) is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his fabulous bowling performance. He says he was trying to keep things simple and bowl to a plan. He feels that the credit actually goes to the batters who did well to get them to a good total. When asked about what they have been doing well recently he says that he knows it is a cliche but the answer is that they keep it simple and try doing what they are good at. Mentions how every teammates success is enjoyed by every other menber and it is good for the team that they have so many options. When asked if he was hoping for Lungi Ngidi to take the catch for his last wicket, he says that it was the other way as he was hoping for Ngidi would get a wicket towards the end so that he could become the fastest South African to 50 T20I wickets.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Andy Balbirnie won the toss and opted to bowl first which seemed like a good decision as they once again got de Kock out for a low score. However, throughout the South African innings, the Irish bowlers were found guilty of conceding multiple boundaries in one over. Gareth Delany and Josh Little though were excellent, conceding a run-a-ball or less. Contributions right throughout the order apart from de Kock and Rassie van der Dussen got the visitors to an above-par total. During the run chase though, Ireland kept on losing wickets in a bunch and this never allowed them to get any momentum into their innings. Riding on Parnell's fifer, the proteas strolled to a series victory.

Even though the Proteas didn't bat particularly well, they did find the fence with regularity and they have now done the same with the wickets while bowling. Wayne Parnell gave them a dream start, picking up two wickets in the second over of the innings and he then came back in later on to pick up a five-wicket haul, a rare feat in this format. The spinners were brilliant too and Dwaine Pretorius got wickets at the right times. Everyone contributed with the ball and even though they couldn't quite wrap up proceedings in style, it was a thoroughly professional performance in the field from the Proteas.

Ireland knew heading into the break that the wicket wasn't a 180-run plus wicket and they had given away a few if not many extra runs with the ball. And, they once again got off on the wrong foot as their skipper departed really cheaply. One wicket became two and then three inside the Powerplay even after some brute force shown by Paul Stirling. Harry Tector showed a bit of consistency and stitched together a stand with Curtis Campher but once Campher fell, Ireland folded like a pack of cards until Barry McCarthy showed some fight and took the opposition bowlers to the cleaners. McCarthy brought the margin of defeat to under 50 runs but Ireland have still suffered a heavy loss.

This has been a totally dominant performance from the Proteas. They have made short work of a long Irish batting order and have sealed the series 2-0! There was a bit of a delay in bundling out the opposition but they have been the better team by a country mile.

OUT! CAUGHT! Aiden Markram is not dropping this one and Barry McCarthy's cameo comes to an end! Dwaine Pretorius continues bowling short and angles the ball into the batter, Barry McCarthy pulls hard but does not time this well as it floats towards deep mid-wicket. Aiden Markram takes a good catch running to his right and makes it look really easy! That brings an end to Ireland's innings and they have lost by 44 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Dwaine Pretorius

Commentary.Commentary: This is short as well and follows the batter as he looks to make room down leg. Josh Little slashes at this and hits it to long on for a single.

Keshav Maharaj seems to have injured his knee as he went in for the catch and seems to be struggling out there. The physio is out on the field to have a look, hope he is fine. Everything seems fine and we are good to continue.

DROPPED! The game should have been over! Dwaine Pretorius bangs this in short and outside off, Barry McCarthy comes down the wicket and skies the ball toward long on. Keshav Maharaj gets under this one and misses a sitter. Hits his knees as it goes through his palms and he is down in pain.
Dwaine Pretorius bowls this on a good length and angling into the pads, Josh Little flicks this towards deep square leg for a single.
Dwaine Pretorius goes full and angling down leg, Barry McCarthy goes to swing and misses. Hits his pads and rolls towards short third man for a leg bye.
Good length, outside off and slower in pace, Little looks to guide it past the keeper but misses.
Slower and shorter, around off, this is pulled off the inside edge towards short fine leg for a single.
SIX! Pace on and McCarthy takes full advantage. This is on a shortish length and outside off, McCarthy fetches it and pulls it hard and flat over the cow corner fence for a maximum.
And again! Fuller and around off, no pace offered by Nigidi. Barry McCarthy goes a bit too hard at it and loses his shape as he misses the ball yet again.
Smartly bowled! This is on a fullish length and outside off, Ngidi takes all the pace off the ball. McCarthy has a swipe across the line but gets beaten for the lack of pace this time.
A length ball, well outside off, Barry McCarthy has a wild swing at it but misses it completely.
FOUR! Josh Little tickles one down fine! Tabraiz Shamsi goes full outside off once again. Josh Little takes out the reverse sweep and gets a glove past short third man for a boundary!
Flights this full and well outside off, Barry McCarthy lifts this towards long off and does not connect well. Lands short of the fielder as they take a single.

FOUR! Barry McCarthy flights this full on leg stump, Barry McCarthy hits this across the line of the ball and gets this to deep mid-wicket for another four runs! This is proving to be quite entertaining.
Tabraiz Shamsi flights this full and on leg, Barry McCarthy looks to heave this leg side and mistimes it towards deep square leg for a couple of well-taken runs.
This is flighted full outside off, Josh Little looks to defend and gets an inside edge towards square leg for a single.
WIDE! Full and turning down leg side, Josh Little looks to work this fine and misses. The umpire calls this one wide.
Tabraiz Shamsi serves this shot and in line with the stumps, Barry McCarthy pulls this to deep square leg for a single.

This is short and wide outside off, Barry McCarthy continues to go hard at the ball and gets a thick outside edge high in the air and it lands in the vacant deep backward point region. Takes a single and keeps strike. 17 runs have come from this over.

SIX! He seems to want to go down fighting here! Dwaine Pretorius continues bowling on length outside off, Barry McCarthy charges down the wicket and hits this even better as it flies well over the long on fielder for a maximum! What hitting by the pace bowler!

FOUR! Barry McCarthy is putting up quite a show here! Dwaine Pretorius serves this on a length outside off, Barry McCarthy thumps this over the non-striker's head towards the long on fence for another boundary in the over.
Dwaine Pretorius goes back to bowling wide outside off, Barry McCarthy strokes this straight to covers.
FOUR! This has been flicked away! Dwaine Pretorius bowls a low full toss on the pads. Barry McCarthy clips the ball towards deep square leg for a boundary.
WIDE! Bangs this in short and wide outside off, Barry McCarthy charges down the wicket and slashes at it. It is too wide and the umpire raises his arms to indicate it.
WIDE! Really wide outside off and full. This is well beyond the tram line and is called wide.
Dwaine Pretorius serves this full and outside off, Barry McCarthy swings hard and misses as it just beats his outside edge.
Short ball outside off, Josh Little sways away and leaves this one alone. What a bowling effort from Wayne Parnell as he ends his quota of four.
Goes 'round the wicket to the new batter and angles the ball in from outside off, Josh Little fends this towards cover.
Josh Little is the last man in for Ireland.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Wayne Parnell has his fifth! What an unbelievable catch behind the wicket by Quinton de Kock! Wayne Parnell bowls this full and angles this into the batter, Andy McBrine comes forward to play this along the line of the delivery. The ball straightens after pitching and gets a faint edge towards the keeper. Quinton de Kock is moving to the right and sees the edge last moment. Dives full length to his left and takes a breathtaking catch! Ireland have lost their ninth wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Wayne Parnell

Commentary.Commentary: Serves this full and just outside off, Andy Balbirnie fends this back towards the bowler's right.
Goes short this time and angles this into the batter, Barry McCarthy mistimes his pull towards deep square leg for a run.
Wayne Parnell begins with a full delivery in line with the stumps, Andy Balbirnie digs this out to long on for a single.
Length ball, outside off, this is played through cover-point for a single.
Barry McCarthy walks out to face a hat-trick delivery.

OUT! CAUGHT! Two in two now for Dwaine Pretorius and he will be on a hat-trick next ball. This is on a shorter length and well outside off, Mark Adair goes after it and carves it uppishly. The ball flies down towards the point fence. Heinrich Klaasen from deep backward point runs to his right and dives in to take a brilliant catch. Mark Adair departs for a low score and South Africa are just two wicket away from victory.
Commentary.Howout: c Heinrich Klaasen b Dwaine Pretorius

Commentary.Commentary: Andy McBrine makes his way out to the crease with the task seeming quite impossible now.

OUT! TAKEN! Dwaine Pretorius gets in on the wicket-taking action and Ireland are now 7 down! This is over off stump, on a hard length and George Dockrell looks to loft it straight down the ground. The bat turns in his hands and ball goes off the splice of the bat, looping up to the left of mid off. David Miller over there slides to his left and takes the catch.
Commentary.Howout: c David Miller b Dwaine Pretorius

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Fuller and angling into the pads, Mark Adair goes back instead of going forward and gets pinged on the back leg. The ball rolls towards backward point and the batters get a leg bye.
Length again, pushed wider and hugging the tramline outside the off stump. Adair has a slash at it but doesn't connect.
Around the top of off, Dockrell pushes it out towards mid off for a quick single.
Dwaine Pretorius comes back into the attack having just bowled one over for 11 runs.
Banged in short and around middle, Mark Adair pulls it towards deep mid-wicket and picks up a couple of runs.
length ball, angling on the pads, this is flicked away through square leg for one.
Mark Adair is the new batter making his way out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust and for the second time tonight, Wayne Parnell gets a double-strike. This is banged in short and at a good height, angling into the body. Harry Tector looks to take it on and goes for the pull. Tector gets hurried on and the ball goes off the top edge, skying around the point region. Lungi Ngidi from short third man calls it early and runs towards it to take a simple catch. Parnell has his fourth and Ireland are fading away real fast.
Commentary.Howout: c Lungi Ngidi b Wayne Parnell

Commentary.Commentary: Dockrell is off the mark in his 100th T20I game! Back of a length, around off, this is tapped towards cover for a single.
George Dockrell has joined Harry Tector in the middle. He will have to play quite a cameo here to take Ireland home.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Curtis Campher tries to be too cute now and pays the price. Slower delivery, over middle stump, Campher tries to reverse sweep it into the third man fence but is beaten for the lack of pace. The ball takes a faint edge on its way to the keeper and Quinton de Kock makes no mistake behind the sticks.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Wayne Parnell

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Good length, angling into the body. Curtis Campher steps down the track and makes a bit of room before powering it right back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Wayne Parnell has been brought back into the attack. He has conceded 20 runs in his 2 overs and taken a couple of wickets.
Maharaj darts this one in on off stump, Tevtor can only manage to jam it back towards the bowler.
WIDE! This is spilled way beyond the tramline outside off, no shot offered.
WIDE! Floated, full and wide outside off, just a bit too wide for the umpire's liking.
Beaten once again! This is very full and around off, Tector looks to get underneath it and loft it straight back but misses.
Well bowled! Slows it up, bowls it fuller and outside off, Tevtor looks to loft it over cover but is beaten.
FOUR! Well struck! In the stumps, Harry Tector plays the slog sweep and gets it well in front of mid-wicket as the ball rockets into the fence.
On the pads, this is flicked away down to fine leg for just another single.
Maharaj sees Tector stepping out and bowls it shorter and wider. Tector slaps it straight to deep cover for a run.
Hit hard but for just a single. This is around off, Harry Tector advances and drills it down to long off for just a single.
On a length and outside off, Campher cuts it through cover for a single.
A hint of flight on this occasion, around off, Tector gets inside the line of the ball and sweeps hard and low towards deep backward square leg for one more.
Floated up, around off, this is swept away in front of square on the leg side for a run.
Half an appeal for LBW but there might have been some glove involved. Tossed up, full and around off, Campher reaches out and tries to paddle it fine. The ball goes off the gloves and onto the pads.
On the shorter side and turning into the pads, Tector goes on the back foot and works it behind square on the leg side for a single.

Drinks break! Ireland are reeling at the moment, having lost four crucial wickets but a big stand here and things could change. South Africa though will be very content at the moment and their bowlers have done an excellent job of picking up wickets at regular intervals. Still, 113 runs are required off 60 balls and the hosts will need to pull off a miracle here if they are to level the series.
Keshav Maharaj fires this one full and wide outside off, Harry Tector has to reach for it as he thumps it towards long off for a single to keep strike. Just 5 runs of the over.
Keshav Maharaj bowls this slower in the air and full outside off, Curtis Campher reverse sweep this straight to short third man but gets a run.
Around off, Harry Tector makes room and plays it towards the cover region for one more.
This is fuller and angling into the pads, Tector fails to work it away.
Flatter again, outside off, Campher slaps it towards deep cover and picks up a single.
Quicker and flatter, sliding into the pads, this is tucked away past square leg for a single.
Goes full on the pads, Harry Tector works this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! This one has been put away! Tabraiz Shamsi serves this short and in line with the stumps and Harry Tector gets low to pull this towards deep square leg for a boundary.
Flighted full outside off, Curtis Campher works this through covers for another run.
This is a fraction short and in line with the stumps, Harry Tector works the ball towards mid-wicket and takes a single.
Goes full once again and angling into the pads, Harry Tector clips this towards fine leg and they run well to pick up a couple of runs.
Full and spinning into the batter, Curtis Campher goes forward but the ball comes in sharply and beats his bat. Hits his body and rolls to the offside for a single.
On a shorter length and heading for middle, Curtis Campher knocks this to the right of point for a single and keeps strike.
SIX! BOOM! This one is out of here! On middle, Curtis Campher dances down the track and thumps it right back over the bowler's head and into the sightscreen for a maximum.
This is short once again and angling in. Harry Tector cuts this late towards point and takes a single.
WIDE! Keshav Maharaj sees Harry Tector makes room leg side, he fires a full delivery wide outside off. Beyond the tram line and called wide.
Flatter delivery, around off, this is cut away towards deep point for a couple of runs.
This is short and angling into the stumps, Curtis Campher looks to make room but gets cramped for space as he knocks the ball towards point for a single.
Keshav Maharaj fired one in full and just going down leg, Curtis Campher goes across to sweep and misses. Just misses the leg stump by a bit.
Keshav Maharaj (1-0-1-0) is back on.
Tabraiz Shamsi serves this short and turning down leg, Harry Tector rocks back and pulls this to the right of short fine leg towards deep backward square leg for a brace.
Goes full once again and outside off, Curtis Campher goes for the sweep and drags the ball towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted full outside off stump this time. Curtis Campher fends the ball towards cover.
Tabraiz Shamsi flights this full and pitching on leg, Curtis Campher looks to fend and gets beaten on the inside edge as it hits his pads. Hige appeal once again but this will be going down leg.
Curtis Campher makes his way to the crease.

OUT! LBW! Gareth Delany's stay at the crease for just two balls and it's once again Tabraiz Shamsi who sends him packing. This is on a length and around off, it is the regular chinaman delivery and turning into the right-hander. Delany looks to work it leg side but gets squared up and gets rapped on the pads. There is a huge shout for LBW and it has been given! Gareth Delany has been adjudged out by the on-field umpire but after some discussion, has gone for the review. No spike on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows wickets as umpire's call as the ball is hitting the top of off. The original decision stands.
Tabraiz Shamsi starts with a full delivery and turning down leg, Gareth Delany looks to clip this and misses. It hits the pads and rolls over to short fine leg.
Tabraiz Shamsi has been brought into the attack now that the Powerplay is done.
A dot to end, just 2 runs and a wicket off it. Back of a length, around off, Tector taps it towards cover-point. At the end of the Powerplay, Ireland are 40/3!
Gareth Delany walks out to the middle with Ireland in a spot of bother.

OUT! TAKEN! A really good take from Aiden Markram and South Africa have the wicket they needed. Lungi Ngidi goes pace off now and serves it on a fullish length, outside off. Paul Stirling looks to go a bit too hard at it and is weway too early in his shot. The ball takes the top edge and goes high over the backward point region. Markram over there runs back and takes it over his shoulders reverse-cup style. Ngidi gets his man and Ireland in a spot of bother here.
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Lungi Ngidi

Commentary.Commentary: Play halted once again! The ball has hit Paul Stirling right in the groin and he is in some pain. Some refreshments come out to give him some time to recover from the blow. He is ready to take strike now.

Ouch, that must have hurt! This is delivered on a hard length and slanted into leg stump. Paul Stirling looks to pull it away but gets hurried on and misses. The ball goes on to hit him right in the groin region and Stirling is down in some pain.
Very full and wide again, Tector reaches out and plays it towards cover for a single.
Full and wide, Tector looks to cover drive but chops it back towards the keeper.

Leg bye! Ngidi starts off with a good-length delivery, around the hips. Stirling looks to work it away leg side but misses. The ball goes off the thigh pads and towards backward square leg. The batters sneak in a leg bye.
Lungi Ngidi (1-0-6-0) to bowl the last over of the Powerplay.
Around middle and leg, tucked away towards mid-wicket for an easy single.
FOUR! A short ball, down leg, Paul Stirling has enough time to just help it on its way, behind square on the leg side and for a boundary.
Around off, this is hit hard and to the left of the man at mid off. The batters scamper through for a single, good running.

Slight halt! Harry Tector seems to have done his wrist some damage playing that shot. His hands come off the bat straight away. He has been having issues with his wrist. Physio is called out to have a look. He seems okay though and play is set to resume.
FOUR! Full and angling down the leg stump, Harry Tector backs away and absolutely drills it back past the bowler and through mid off for a boundary.
Length again, angling it into the pads, Stirling gets an inside edge. The ball goes off the pads and rolls onto the leg side. Single taken.
Starts off with a lovely delivery. Perfect length, in that channel around off and just nibbling away a touch. Paul Stirling looks to have a dab at it but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Dwaine Pretorius has been asked to bowl the penultimate over of the Powerplay.
A single to end the over, 18 coming off it. Full and around off, Stirling comes forward and drives it towards mid on for one.
FOUR! Sweetly timed! Length ball, outside off, Stirling just slaps it away past point for a boundary.
SIX! Short again, on leg stump, Paul Stirling muscles it away flat and hard, over the square leg fence for another maximum.
Short of a length, outside off, Stirling cuts it away off the bottom edge towards backward point.

SIX! The first boundary of the Irish innings and it is a big one. Pitched up, right in the slot and on leg stump. Paul Stirling makes a bit of room, freeing his arms and uses brute force to loft it over long on for a maximum.

Direct hit but the batter is well in. Good length, angling across the right-hander. Harry Tector takes a few steps towards the ball and plays it to mid off. Tector sets off for the run and gets inside the crease in time.

Excellent work from Dwaine Pretorius. Pitched up, on the stumps and Paul Stirling lifts it right back over the bowler's head. The fielder from mid on chases it down and pulls the ball back in. Two taken.
Length again, on off, Harry Tector walks towards the ball and drives it straight to mid off for a quick single.
A length ball, outside off, Tector taps it towards cover-point.
Full, on middle and leg, Paul Stirling clips it away in front of mid-wicket and looks for two but has to settle for just the single.
Good running! At the stumps and pushed away firmly to the right of mid on. Harry Tector takes off immediately and gets through for a single.
Good length, over middle, pushed away towards mid on.
WIDE! Starts off with a wayward delivery, full and down the leg side. Wide called.
Lungi Ngidi has been brought into the attack after just one over of spin.
No hat-trick! Short and over leg stump, this is worked off hips by Tector down to fine leg for a single. Ireland in early trouble here as they are 3/2 at the end of 2 overs.
Harry Tector walks out to the middle to face the hat-trick ball!

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man and all of a sudden, Wayne Parnell is on a hat-trick! Pitches it up around off, trying to swing it back into the right-hander. Lorcan Tucker looks to drag it and loft it over mid on but gets it off the toe end of the bat. The ball goes uppishly and towards the man at mid on. Dwaine Pretorius takes a comfotable catch around his chest and Tucker departs for a golden duck.
Commentary.Howout: c Dwaine Pretorius b Wayne Parnell

Commentary.Commentary: Lorcan Tucker strides out to the middle. Will be looking to follow up his last innings with a match-winning knock today.

OUT! CAUGHT! A soft, soft dismissal for the Irish skipper and South Africa have the early breakthrough. This is on a hard length and around off, a bit slower as well. Andy Balbirnie looks to play it over the infield on the off side but the ball sticks in the pitch. The ball goes off the leading edge and towards short extra cover where Keshav Maharaj takes a dolly of a catch. Wayne Parnell has drawn first blood here.
Commentary.Howout: c Keshav Maharaj b Wayne Parnell

Commentary.Commentary: Full and wide, this one just keeps on going away from the right-hander. Quinton de Kock with a great take diving to his right, saved a certain boundary there.
Full and straight, Andy Balbirnie plays a straight drive, not well-timed and towards mid on.
Starts off with a full ball, swinging in from middle. Paul Stirling flicks it down to fine leg and picks up a single.
Wayne Parnell to bowl from the opposite end.
Goes back to bowling short and pitches this outside off, Andy Balbirnie hits this straight to cover. Just one run from the first over and South Africa have started well here.
Goes full this time and in line with the stumps, Andy Balbirnie nudges this towards mid on and once again not sure whether to take a single. Decides against it.
This is short and angled into the stumps, Andy Balbirnie rocks back and punches the ball towards cover.
This is full and outside off, Andy Balbirnie taps the ball towards mid off and looks for a single. Changes his mind at the last moment.
Quicker delivery angling down leg, Andy Balbirnie looks to play this leg side and skids onto his pads as he misses.
Keshav Maharaj begins with a full delivery just outside off, Paul Stirling knocks this wide of long off for a single.
